To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the damage to the hippocampal neurons induced by 5- and 7. 5-min-long episodes with anoxia is manifested as an irreversible reduction in the amplitude of the field EPSP; (b) the damage to neurons is prevented by antagonists of the NMDA receptors and by a blocker of the AMPA receptors combined with a local anesthesia; (c) chronic introduction of antidepressants into experimental animals results in a noticeable weakening of the impairments induced in
the anoxic damage of the hippocampus can be prevented by the chronic administration of antidepressants.

the anoxic damage of the hippocampus, as well as its modifications resulting from chronic antidepressant treatment, are determined by the balance of activities of the NMDA and AMPA receptors, as well as of the Ca2+ channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using the model of OGD-induced injury of hippocampal neurons for studying the molecular mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects induced by antidepressants.
the possibility of application of antidepressant drugs in the therapy of ischemic brain diseases.
the mechanisms of neuroprotective actions exerted by antidepressants under the influence of OGD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic antidepressants influence the anoxic damage of hippocampal neurons in a complex manner and, as a result, can be considered as a factor of neuroprotection.
the neuroprotective effect of the antidepressants is determined by their influence on the expression of neurotrophic factors, which in turn modulates the activity of NMDARs.
antidepressant drugs are able to exert neuroprotective activities with respect to the early damage to the hippocampal neurons under conditions of oxygen/glucose deficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antidepressants can be used as a neuroprotective agent in cases of acute brain ischemia.

the neuroprotective effects exerted by antidepressants are determined by the ability of the drugs to intensify the expression of neurotrophic proteins and by the ability of these proteins to decrease the functional activity of receptors for glutamate and calcium channels.

the neuroprotective actions exerted by chronic administration of antidepressants are determined by the activation of the expression of neurotrophic factors, which are capable of decreasing the functional activity of receptors of glutamate, as a result of the increase of the level of phosphoprotein phosphates in neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neuroprotective actions exerted by antidepressants with respect the anoxic damage of hippocampal neurons are not limited to the early period of their action, but also extend to the chronic period of their influence.
antidepressants can be used to treat patients with anoxic brain damage, and the most effective of these drugs are imipramine and fluoxetine.
antidepressants, when administered chronically in therapeutic doses, may be used as a means of preventing or attenuating damage to the hippocampal neurons in the case of acute anoxic insults.
